drop.reason: Spatial transcriptomics of the tumour microenvironment; the finding is cellular architecture, not the tumour genome.
Clinical gene-therapy safety report; genomics serves an adverse-event investigation in a treatment study.
Software paper (SComatic) for calling somatic mutations in single-cell data.
Sequencing-technology paper (CODEC); the result is the assay, not a cancer-genome finding.
Bacterial adhesin mechanism; near-duplicate of the more cited colibactin mutagenesis papers kept.
Immune-checkpoint-inhibitor efficacy study; clinical treatment outcome, genotype only as a selector.
Debut of a single-molecule sequencing method; the result is the technology's resolution of mismatches.
Software paper (MuSiCal) for mutational signature extraction.
Software paper (Severus) for long-read somatic SV calling.
Methodological benchmark of short- versus long-read SV detection rather than a tumour-biology finding.
Subcellular protein assembly map resource in a cell line; not a cancer-genome finding.
APOBEC3A/B substrate biochemistry; near-duplicate of the APOBEC mutagenesis papers already kept.
Epigenomic reprogramming and therapeutic vulnerability of ARID1A-mutant tumours; genomic alteration is the entry point, not the result.
Exposure-hazard study of a UV device in cultured cells; no tumour genomes analysed.
Proteomics-led subtyping of colorectal cancer; genomic alterations are secondary to proteome-based classes.
Germline mutation spectrum across mammals; an evolutionary-genomics result, not cancer genomics.
Germline structural variants as inherited risk factors, not somatic tumour-genome findings.
Technical validation of FFPE whole-genome sequencing for clinical use.
Methylation-clock tool for estimating mitotic age; the result is the counter.
Mouse model resource characterised by immune microenvironment, not tumour genome analysis.
Methods paper for haplotype-resolved cancer-genome reconstruction, demonstrated on one cell line.
Analysis pipeline (HAPI) for detecting enhancer hijacking; the deliverable is the method.
Perspective/commentary on whether to test children for adult-onset predisposition genes.
Deep-learning tool (MuAt) for tumour typing from mutation data.
Therapeutic development: CRISPR-based oncolysis exploiting a mutational signature.
Protein-coding consequence of smoking and APOBEC signatures; near-duplicate of the signature-aetiology papers kept.
Yeast model of inverted-repeat-driven rearrangement; no tumour genomes.
Chromatin architecture and enhancer connectome survey; the result is 3D regulatory structure rather than genome alteration.
Enhancer-activity profiling for therapeutic vulnerabilities in cholangiocarcinoma; epigenomic, not genomic, result.
Germline de novo mutation rates in repair-deficient families; germline rather than tumour genome.
Prevalence and clinical management of germline predisposition variants in paediatric cancer.
Homologous-recombination-deficiency classification from exomes; methodological and clinical rather than a genome-biology finding.
APOBEC and tumour evolution in smokers; near-duplicate of the more cited lung and APOBEC papers kept.
Method paper (GTAC) coupling genotyping with chromatin accessibility in single cells.
Cell-biological mechanism of mutant MLL4 mislocalisation; the result is protein behaviour, not a genomic finding.
Patient-derived xenograft model resource for CLL and Richter transformation.
Immune infiltration and treatment response in bilateral breast cancer; clinical outcome study.
Methylation signatures linked to immune microenvironment and immunotherapy response; epigenomic/immunological result.
Enhancer hijacking from 3D maps in colorectal cancer; near-duplicate of the 3D-genome cluster.
3D chromatin rewiring at relapse; near-duplicate of the 3D-genome cluster.
Single-cell transcriptomic clonal evolution in myeloma; expression-based rather than a genome finding.
Mismatch-repair mechanism in cultured cell lines; no tumour genomes analysed.
Yeast deletion screen for modifiers of APOBEC3B mutagenesis; near-duplicate of the APOBEC cluster.
HPV integration rearrangements in cervical cancer; near-duplicate of the HPV-integration paper kept.
Synthetic-lethal drug-target discovery for 8p-deleted tumours; the result is a therapeutic target.
SMC5/6 replication-stress mechanism; near-duplicate of the APOBEC cluster and mechanistic rather than genomic.
Clinical tumour testing for biallelic loss in germline-variant carriers; diagnostic rather than genome-landscape finding.
Xenograft model resource characterisation; genomic fidelity of PDXs rather than tumour-genome biology.
Centrosome-dependent double-strand-break repair; cell biology outside cancer genomics.
Purine metabolism and m6A regulation in hepatocellular carcinoma; metabolic/epitranscriptomic result.

notes: The kept 50 are tumour-genome findings: mutational signatures and their aetiologies (tobacco, UV, APOBEC, colibactin, chemotherapy, defective repair), somatic mutation and clonal expansion in normal and preneoplastic tissue, structural variation and chromothripsis, aneuploidy and copy-number evolution, ecDNA, large WGS and multi-omic cohorts (100,000 Genomes, paediatric pan-cancer, lung adenocarcinoma, urothelial, thyroid, head and neck), and single-cell clonal evolution. Dropped are algorithm, sequencing-technology and benchmark papers, germline-predisposition and clinical-testing studies, treatment-outcome and model-resource papers, and lower-cited near-duplicates within the APOBEC, colibactin, HPV-integration and 3D-genome clusters. The set is thin on 3D genome architecture, cancer epigenomics and non-coding driver discovery, leans heavily on mutational-process work from a few large sequencing consortia, and covers haematological and paediatric tumours less than epithelial cancers.
